approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Colorado Natural Gas customer for the service and measure receiving the incentive.
For a prescriptive rebate, install currently qualifying equipment or building-envelope work and retain the required invoice, model, efficiency, and contractor documentation.

For a custom commercial or industrial project, contact the program before installation, execute the participation documents, complete the required audit or savings review, and receive an incentive reservation.
Complete the approved work and permit post-installation inspection or savings verification when required.
Submit the claim while the applicable program budget remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current prescriptive rebates use published eligibility and documentation rules, while custom projects use an audit, reservation, and verification pathway rather than competitive ranking. A compliant project is generally payable while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Colorado Natural Gas currently lists residential prescriptive rebates and a commercial custom process requiring early participation, savings review, incentive reservation, completion, and inspection.

approvalRequirements: Own or improve an eligible existing residential property in Colorado.
Use the financing for a currently eligible RENU improvement and confirm program scope for any mapped measure not expressly listed in the current product description.
Select a RENU-authorized contractor and apply through a participating credit union or lender.
Pass borrower credit, income, project, and lender underwriting requirements.
Execute the approved loan documents before installation or disbursement and complete the project under the lender and program terms.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: RENU is financing rather than an automatic rebate. Approval depends on borrower underwriting, an eligible project scope, an authorized contractor, and execution of the loan before work; some mapped measures are not expressly identified on the current program page.
reviews.evidenceText: The current RENU product finances listed residential energy improvements through authorized contractors and participating lenders, subject to credit and project approval.

approvalRequirements: Register the builder for the current program year and submit the required builder participation application and tax documentation.
Construct an eligible new home in Colorado Springs Utilities service territory.
Use an independent certified RESNET HERS rater and meet the current maximum HERS Index requirement.
Obtain the applicable LEED certification when claiming the LEED incentive component.
Submit the completed home report, rating, certifications, and other required records within the program deadline after final inspection.
Permit utility inspection or verification and apply while program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The builder program uses objective annual enrollment, HERS performance, certification, and documentation requirements. A properly registered and verified qualifying home is likely to receive the published incentive, subject to available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Current builder materials require annual registration, an independent HERS rating, timely post-construction reporting, and supporting certification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible Colorado Springs Utilities business account for the utility service associated with the measure.
Select a currently offered qualifying HVAC, water-efficiency, irrigation, or custom measure and satisfy its technical specifications.
Obtain program approval before purchase or installation for custom projects and any other pathway identified as preapproval-required.
Use licensed contractors, permits, assessments, or inspections where the selected measure requires them.
Submit the current application with itemized invoices, equipment data, savings calculations, and completion documentation as applicable.
Permit post-installation inspection or verification and apply while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current business offerings combine objective prescriptive rebates with preapproved custom pathways. A qualifying project that follows the correct sequence is generally likely to be paid after documentation and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Colorado Springs Utilities currently lists business rebates and states that custom projects require approval before purchase, followed by completion records and verification.

approvalRequirements: Have the applicable Colorado Springs Utilities residential account and service at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying product or measure during the applicable program year.
Obtain required permits and final inspection for HVAC, heat-pump water-heater, or other permit-controlled work.
Submit the current rebate application with itemized receipts, model and efficiency information, and contractor documentation by the stated deadline.
Permit inspection or verification when requested and apply while program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The residential rebates are generally formula-based and use published equipment, service, permit, receipt, and submission requirements. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Current residential rules require eligible utility service, current-year installation, receipts and equipment records, timely filing, and permits or final inspection for specified measures.

approvalRequirements: Be served by Columbia Gas of Kentucky and complete the current low-income program screening through the designated community-action administrator.
Provide household, income, account, occupancy, and property documentation requested during eligibility review.
Have an existing furnace that the program determines is old, nonworking, or inefficient and appropriate for replacement.
Receive program authorization before the furnace is replaced.
Complete any required assessment, contractor access, installation, and final verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program may replace an eligible low-income customer's qualifying furnace at no cost, but the award depends on household screening, furnace condition, program authorization, and available program capacity rather than a simple post-purchase claim.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia Gas of Kentucky directs customers to eligibility screening for possible no-cost replacement of an old, nonworking, or inefficient furnace.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Gas of Virginia residential customer with an existing home and the required natural-gas service or primary heating configuration for the selected measure.
Purchase and install currently qualifying equipment during the applicable program period.
Meet the published model, efficiency, installation, and contractor requirements.
Submit the completed rebate application with invoice, proof of payment, account information, and equipment documentation by the deadline.
Permit inspection or verification when selected and apply while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: WarmWise rebates are based on published customer, equipment, installation, and claim requirements rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying complete claim is likely to be paid, subject to verification and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Virginia residential rebate page lists qualifying gas equipment and thermostats, documentation requirements, possible inspection, and limited first-come funding.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Rural Electric Association commercial or agricultural member with the qualifying electric service at the project site.
Contact the cooperative before purchase or installation to confirm the current measure, incentive, and required case-by-case review.
Obtain any required preapproval or incentive commitment before starting the project.
Install qualifying equipment in accordance with the approved scope and applicable codes.
Submit the current application with invoices, model data, technical documentation, and completion records.
Permit inspection or verification and apply while program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative states that commercial and agricultural rebates are evaluated case by case and remain subject to available funds. Eligibility therefore permits review but does not make an award automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia REA currently lists commercial and agricultural efficiency rebates, with applications reviewed case by case and paid only after required documentation and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Rural Electric Association residential member with qualifying service at the installation address.
Install a currently listed qualifying HVAC, thermostat, duct, water-heating, weatherization, or appliance measure within the active program period.
Use a qualified contractor and meet the current equipment, testing, code, and installation requirements.
Obtain preapproval before multifamily weatherization, multiple-project combinations, or any other measure identified as preapproval-required.
Submit the current application with invoices and technical records within the measure-specific filing period.
Permit program inspection or verification and apply while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current residential forms publish objective equipment, contractor, timing, and documentation rules. Standard qualifying claims are likely to be paid, while specified multifamily or combined projects require advance approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Columbia REA residential materials list HVAC, duct, thermostat, water-heating, appliance, and weatherization rebates with filing deadlines and preapproval for specified projects.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia River PUD commercial customer with qualifying electric service at the project site.
Contact the PUD for a project review or energy evaluation before purchase when the selected measure requires advance coordination.
Install a currently qualifying lighting, HVAC, thermostat, refrigeration, kitchen, insulation, or related measure meeting the current specifications.
Use qualified contractors and comply with applicable permits and codes.
Submit the required application, invoices, model data, and completion documentation.
Permit inspection or verification before final payment when requested and apply while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The PUD offers current business efficiency assistance and rebates through defined measure pathways. A qualifying project that is coordinated as required and passes documentation and verification is generally likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia River PUD currently offers business evaluations and measure-specific efficiency incentives, with project coordination, qualifying equipment, documentation, and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Rural Electric Association agricultural member with qualifying electric service.
Submit the variable-frequency-drive project for cooperative review and obtain written preapproval before purchase or installation.
Provide the required equipment, motor-load, operating-hour, cost, and projected-savings information.
Install the approved drive and associated controls in accordance with the approved scope and applicable code.
Submit invoices, completion records, and any required operating or commissioning information.
Permit post-installation verification and apply while current program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current variable-frequency-drive incentive requires project-specific preapproval, technical information, cost limits, and post-installation documentation. Approval is therefore project- and budget-dependent rather than automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia REA's current agricultural variable-frequency-drive form requires advance approval, project data, invoices, and verification, with payment subject to program limits and funds.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Rural Electric Association commercial member with qualifying electric service at the project site.
Contact the cooperative before purchase or installation to confirm the current equipment category and case-by-case incentive review.
Obtain any required preapproval or incentive commitment before starting work.
Install qualifying HVAC or thermostat equipment in accordance with the approved scope and applicable code.
Submit the application with invoices, model and efficiency documentation, and completion records.
Permit inspection or verification and apply while program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Commercial rebates are evaluated case by case and remain subject to available funds. A technically eligible project may receive an award, but eligibility alone does not establish likely payment before project review.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia REA currently lists commercial HVAC and thermostat rebates but states that commercial incentives are reviewed case by case and require supporting project documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Rural Electric Association residential member with qualifying service at the installation address.
Install a currently listed qualifying HVAC, duct, water-heating, weatherization, window, or appliance measure within the active program period.
Use a qualified contractor and meet current equipment, testing, code, and installation specifications.
Obtain preapproval before multifamily weatherization, multiple-project combinations, or any other measure identified as preapproval-required.
Submit the current application with invoices and technical records within the measure-specific filing period.
Permit inspection or verification and apply while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative's current residential forms use objective equipment, contractor, filing, and documentation rules. Standard compliant claims are likely to be paid, while specified multifamily or combined projects require advance approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Columbia REA residential materials support multiple HVAC, duct, weatherization, water-heating, window, and appliance measures with deadlines, documentation, and specified preapproval conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Water & Light commercial electric customer at the project site.
Request the required preauthorization and site review before purchasing or installing lighting or HVAC equipment.
Install equipment meeting the current efficiency, sizing, control, and contractor requirements.
Obtain applicable permits and complete any required duct, commissioning, or installation inspection.
Submit invoices, specifications, completion records, and the final incentive request within the applicable deadline.
Permit final inspection and apply while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current commercial lighting and HVAC programs use a defined preauthorization, installation, documentation, and inspection sequence rather than competitive selection. An approved compliant project is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia Water & Light currently requires advance approval for commercial lighting and HVAC incentives, followed by qualifying installation, invoices, and inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Water & Light residential electric customer at the project address.
Use the applicable current pathway for HVAC, weatherization, water heating, windows, or Level 2 electric-vehicle charging.
For Home Performance measures, complete the initial energy assessment and obtain recommendations before starting work.
Use qualified contractors, obtain required permits, and install equipment or improvements meeting current specifications.
Submit invoices, assessment or testing results, equipment data, and the final application by the applicable deadline.
Permit post-installation inspection or verification and apply while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current residential offerings use objective measure-specific requirements. Home Performance work requires an assessment before installation, and qualifying completed projects are generally likely to be paid after documentation and inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia Water & Light currently lists residential HVAC, Home Performance, electrification, water-heating, insulation, window, and Level 2 charging pathways with assessment, permit, documentation, and inspection rules.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Water & Light residential electric customer at the installation address.
Install currently qualifying central air-conditioning, air-source heat-pump, or eligible geothermal equipment.
Use a qualified contractor, obtain the required permit, and meet current sizing, efficiency, and installation specifications.
Submit the rebate application, paid invoice, equipment records, and permit information within the current filing period.
Permit utility inspection or verification and apply while funds remain.
Confirm eligibility through a separate current program before treating an efficient pump replacement as covered by this HVAC rebate.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official page supports air-conditioning, air-source heat-pump, and eligible geothermal rebates, but it does not substantiate the mapped efficient-pump replacement. The documented HVAC measures are likely after review, while the full legacy mapping needs reconciliation.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Columbia Water & Light materials document residential air-conditioning, heat-pump, and eligible geothermal rebates with permit, invoice, deadline, and inspection requirements; efficient pump replacement is not documented there.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Columbia Water & Light electric customer with a qualifying solar project at the service address.
Consult the utility and submit the applicable solar rebate, net-metering, and interconnection materials before installation or system energization.
Use qualifying photovoltaic modules, inverters, metering, and licensed installation meeting current technical and code requirements.
Complete permits, inspection, interconnection approval, and permission to operate.
Submit final invoices, system data, and production or completion documentation required for the rebate.
Confirm another current program before treating window film or general submetering and energy monitoring as eligible solar-rebate measures.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program supports qualifying solar photovoltaic systems through rebate and interconnection review, but the mapped window-film and general monitoring measures are not solar-rebate measures. The opportunity is therefore only partially aligned with the target mapping.
reviews.evidenceText: Columbia Water & Light currently requires solar-project coordination, interconnection, inspection, and final documentation; its solar pages do not document window-film or general submetering incentives.

approvalRequirements: The former standalone Maryland Combined Heat and Power grant intake is inactive, so no current application can be approved under that program.
For a future or successor solicitation, confirm that the applicant, site, CHP technology, fuel, and project costs meet the new notice's eligibility rules.
Submit a complete application during an open funding period and pass any technical, cost-effectiveness, scoring, and ranking review.
Receive a formal award and execute the grant agreement before incurring reimbursable project costs.
Confirm that any biomass or biogas configuration is expressly eligible under the active successor solicitation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Maryland Energy Administration identifies the standalone CHP program as inactive and does not provide a current application pathway. A project could only proceed through a future or successor solicitation with separate selection and agreement requirements.
reviews.evidenceText: The official Maryland page states that the standalone Combined Heat and Power program is inactive and directs interested parties to consider other or successor opportunities.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible ComEd nonresidential account for the installation site.
Purchase a currently qualifying LED lighting product through a participating distributor or other approved instant-discount channel.
Provide the account, installation-site, product, quantity, and customer information required for point-of-sale validation.
Permit the distributor or program to retain claim records and verify installation or eligibility.
Confirm a separate current program before treating a low-flow plumbing fixture as eligible under the lighting-discount offering.
Complete the transaction while instant-discount funds and qualifying products remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current materials support instant discounts for qualifying business lighting through participating market channels, but the mapped low-flow fixture is not a lighting measure. The LED portion is awardable after validation; the full opportunity mapping needs confirmation.
reviews.evidenceText: ComEd's current business channels include instant lighting discounts through participating providers; current evidence does not place low-flow plumbing fixtures in that lighting program.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible ComEd customer with a qualifying distributed-generation or permanently installed storage project.
Submit and obtain approval for the required interconnection application and install compliant smart-inverter and metering equipment.
For storage, meet the current requirement that the system be associated with qualifying distributed generation and satisfy capacity and operational conditions.
Receive permission to operate before final rebate approval where required.
Submit a complete signed rebate application with invoices, proof of payment, equipment data, and interconnection documentation.
Permit inspection or verification when requested.
Confirm separate treatment for community-solar subscriptions or general submetering, which are not documented as direct equipment rebates under this offering.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program provides formula-based rebates for qualifying distributed generation and storage after interconnection and documentation review. The mapped community-solar subscription and general monitoring categories are not direct claimant equipment rebates, so the legacy mapping is only partially supported.
reviews.evidenceText: Current ComEd materials require eligible generation or associated storage, interconnection approval, permission to operate, a complete rebate claim, and possible inspection; community-solar subscriptions are not direct equipment rebates.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible ComEd residential account for the installation or purchase address.
Use the current measure-specific pathway and select equipment or products meeting the applicable efficiency and qualifying-product requirements.
Use a participating retailer, distributor, contractor, or Energy Efficiency Service Provider where the pathway requires one.
Obtain any required preapproval, assessment, or instant-discount validation before purchase or installation.
Submit invoices, equipment data, contractor records, and completion documentation for post-installation claims and permit verification or inspection.
Confirm current eligibility separately for mapped categories not clearly documented in the current residential offering, including any ground-source, low-flow, laundry, or induction measure.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: ComEd currently operates standardized residential product, HVAC, thermostat, lighting, and whole-home pathways. Supported measures are generally likely to receive an incentive after the applicable point-of-sale or contractor review, although several legacy mapped categories need current confirmation.
reviews.evidenceText: Current ComEd materials identify residential lighting, product, thermostat, heating-and-cooling, home-savings, multifamily, and whole-home electrification pathways, with participating-provider and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible ComEd business account and select the correct current pathway for the proposed measure.
Use a participating Energy Efficiency Service Provider, distributor, or other approved market actor when the pathway requires one.
For standard, custom, industrial, retro-commissioning, or other project-based incentives, submit the project before purchase or installation when preapproval is required.
Provide equipment specifications, baseline and savings data, cost information, and other technical documentation requested during review.
Install the approved equipment or measures and submit invoices, completion records, and final savings documentation.
Permit inspection, measurement, or verification and complete the project while program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The 2026 business portfolio includes instant, standard, custom, industrial, refrigeration, HVAC, controls, drives, compressed-air, and retro-commissioning pathways. Awards are generally likely for qualifying projects that follow the correct preapproval or point-of-sale process and pass verification.
reviews.evidenceText: ComEd's current business portfolio covers instant discounts and project-based incentives for lighting, HVAC, controls, refrigeration, drives, compressed air, custom efficiency, and retro-commissioning, subject to pathway-specific approval and verification.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible SDG&E customer site and use the qualifying equipment for an eligible end-use application.
Select equipment appearing on the current Comfortably CA qualified-product list or obtain any required engineering review for a nonstandard or large product.
Purchase through a participating distributor and provide the customer, installation-site, equipment, and contractor information needed for the distributor's claim.
Install the equipment in accordance with program, code, and manufacturer requirements and retain requested records.
Allow the distributor and program administrator to validate the transaction and incentive.
Confirm how much of the distributor incentive will be passed through to the customer because the program does not guarantee a direct customer rebate.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Comfortably CA pays incentives through participating distributors rather than promising a direct rebate to the end customer. A qualifying HVAC transaction may receive a program incentive, but distributor participation, product qualification, available funds, and pass-through terms affect the customer award.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Comfortably CA materials state that incentives are claimed by participating distributors for qualifying products and that any customer price reduction depends on the distributor's pass-through practice.

approvalRequirements: No new FY 2026 application can be submitted because that round has completed selection and agreements have been distributed.
For a future round, be an eligible Maryland commercial or industrial applicant with a project and costs meeting the current funding notice.
Submit a complete application by the future deadline with the required project scope, budget, savings, technical, and organizational documentation.
Pass threshold review, competitive scoring, and rank-order selection within available funds.
Receive a formal award and execute the grant agreement before beginning costs that require pre-agreement authorization.
Confirm that a stand-alone retro-commissioning study is eligible under the future notice rather than assuming eligibility from the legacy record.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The FY 2026 Commercial and Industrial grant round is no longer accepting applications and agreements have been distributed. A future award would require a new solicitation, competitive scoring and ranking, and an executed agreement, so a current new applicant is unlikely to receive an award.
reviews.evidenceText: Maryland's current program page states that FY 2026 award agreements have been distributed and points prospective applicants to a future FY 2027 update; the completed round used competitive scoring and grant agreements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible existing-building customer of a participating utility in Oregon or southwest Washington.
For a standard incentive, install a currently qualifying measure and meet the applicable equipment, contractor, and technical specifications.
Submit the current incentive form with the invoice, tax form, specifications, and other required documentation within the filing period after installation.
For a custom project, contact Energy Trust before purchase or installation, complete the technical analysis, and receive a written incentive offer or preapproval.
Complete the project in accordance with the approved scope and submit final cost and completion records.
Permit post-installation inspection, commissioning, or savings verification and apply while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Energy Trust's current Existing Buildings program provides published standard incentives and a defined custom preapproval path. Qualifying standard claims and preapproved custom projects are generally likely to be paid after complete documentation and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Existing Buildings program distinguishes standard post-installation claims from custom projects requiring early technical review, a written incentive offer, final invoices, and verification.
